Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

eSVD2 1.2.0

The first version intended for CRAN. Everything below is relative to 1.0.1.07, the version on the master branch from April 2026 and the last one installed from GitHub. The development versions 1.0.2 and 1.1.0 in between were never released; their changes are folded in here.

Results differ from 1.0.1.07

Every analysis gives different statistics, p-values and fold changes, for all genes. The reasons, from largest to smallest effect:

  • The nuisance rate is capped. estimate_nuisance() bounds each gene’s Gamma rate (the reciprocal of the over-dispersion) at cap_multiplier times the median of the gene’s library size, with cap_multiplier = 10 by default, and floors it at min_val times the same median. A gene whose counts are no more variable than a Poisson has no finite maximum-likelihood rate; 1.0.1.07 gave such a gene the largest library size (see the next item), its posterior followed the fit, and its statistic was inflated. The cap is a calibration device, and the documentation says so. cap_multiplier = Inf removes it. eSVD() and eSVD_helper() take the new argument cap_multiplier.
  • The rate is now the maximum-likelihood estimate. gamma_rate() truncated its search at the largest library size of the gene and returned that bound as if it were the estimate whenever the true maximizer lay above it. The bracket now grows until the maximizer is inside it.
  • A degraded empirical null is no longer silent. Welch statistics are mapped to Gaussian statistics on the log scale, so one strongly up-regulated gene no longer produces an infinite statistic that pushed locfdr onto its crudest fallback for the whole data set. multtest() reports which estimator ran (pvalue_list$method) and warns whenever it is not locfdr. The truncated-Gaussian fallback is Efron’s estimator with the constraint p0 <= 1 restored (without it, 200 draws from N(0, 1) gave a null standard deviation of 2.6), and the moment estimator is corrected for truncation.
  • Two defaults changed. compute_test_per_gene() floors the library size at library_min = 0.1, as eSVD() and compute_posterior() always did, instead of 0.01. estimate_nuisance() on an eSVD object defaults to bool_covariates_as_library = TRUE, as compute_posterior() does and as eSVD() has always passed it; a stage-by-stage analysis run with defaults used to estimate the rate on one library size and compute the posterior on another.
  • The fit is deterministic. The iterative SVD solvers start from a fixed vector, so identical inputs give identical fits and the user’s random seed is not consumed. Two runs of 1.0.1.07 on the same data differed by up to 0.006 in the Welch statistic.

New functions

  • eSVD_helper() wraps eSVD() with the cohort filters of the paper, and filter_cohort() applies them alone: minimum cells per individual, per arm and overall, and minimum individuals per arm. All-zero genes are removed before the fit and reinserted afterwards with NA results; the outcome of every filter is recorded in gene_status and param.
  • compute_log_fold_change() gives each gene a log2 fold change between the case and control individuals and a delta-method standard error for it, on the unit of replication of the individual (as ‘DESeq2’, ‘dreamlet’ and ‘NEBULA’ report it). Both are computed by compute_test_statistic() and compute_test_per_gene() and stored as log2fc_vec and log2fc_se_vec. ?compute_log_fold_change says what the standard error does and does not account for.
  • recompute_pvalue() redoes the posterior, the statistic and the p-values at another cap_multiplier on a fitted object, without fitting again. An object built with bool_diet = TRUE has no counts; pass the Seurat object the analysis was run on, and the counts and covariates are rebuilt and checked against summaries recorded at the fit.
  • plot_nuisance() draws each gene’s rate, in units of its library size, against its mean count, its -log10 p-value or its sparsity, with the cap drawn. plot_fitted_vs_observed() draws the fitted against the observed count per cell and gene, marking the points more than num_sd model standard deviations from the fit. Both need ‘ggplot2’ (and ‘ggrepel’), which are suggested, not required.
  • multtest() and reparameterization_esvd_covariates() are exported by name, with documentation and examples.

Changes that can affect existing code

  • report_results() returns seven columns where it returned four: genes, logFC, logFC_se, log10pvalue, pvalue, pvalue_adj and nuisance_status. Code that reads columns by position breaks.
  • Every gene has a nuisance_status (estimated, capped, boundary or failed), stored as a factor beside nuisance_vec in the fit, with the uncapped estimate in nuisance_mle_vec. The fit and param carry more entries (gene means and sparsity, the library medians, the counts of capped and boundary genes, the variable names eSVD() was called with, the posterior settings, and the individuals of each arm).
  • compute_test_statistic(), compute_pvalue() and compute_test_per_gene() take min_cells_per_individual (default 3), which eSVD() passes through.
  • opt_esvd() on matrices takes nuisance_vec = NULL (meaning 1 for every gene) instead of a vector of NA; four of the seven families consumed the NA inside the objective and failed in the line search.
  • estimate_nuisance(), compute_posterior(), compute_test_statistic() and compute_test_per_gene() overwrite their entries of param when rerun, so a rerun on a changed cohort or setting is recorded.
  • An object saved by 1.0.1.07 still works with report_results() (logFC_se and nuisance_status are NA, with a warning) and is refused by compute_log_fold_change(), recompute_pvalue() and the two plots, which need what 1.2.0 stores.
  • compute_pvalue() on an object built with eSVD(bool_diet = TRUE) stops with a message saying the p-values were already computed by compute_test_per_gene(); it used to fail inside .compute_df().

Correctness fixes

Each of these was a silent wrong answer in 1.0.1.07.

  • initialize_esvd() zeroes NA counts in sparse matrices too (a single NA in a dgCMatrix errored inside ‘glmnet’), keeps the library-size offset in the single-covariate stats::glm fallback (a design with only the case-control indicator was initialized without depth adjustment), and refuses all-zero genes instead of mis-fitting them.
  • reparameterization_esvd_covariates() regresses on the design matrix directly instead of through stats::lm(x ~ ., data = ...), which rewrote non-syntactic covariate names such as "Diagnosis_ASD (severe)" (a subscript error) and returned NA coefficients for aliased columns that propagated into z_mat and every posterior. The identification step floors an eigenvalue at or below tol instead of inverting it (an exact zero gave Inf, a rounding-error negative gave NaN).
  • opt_esvd() counts failed Newton line searches in C++ and raises one R warning at the end, instead of Rcpp::warning() from inside a C++ frame (which can skip destructors under options(warn = 2)), and stops with a message when the objective becomes non-finite. Its verbose output printed nothing useful.
  • gamma_rate() and log_gamma_rate() check that x, mu and s have the same length (a shorter input was an out-of-bounds read).
  • The C++ data loader rejects an unsupported matrix type on entry instead of returning a null pointer that failed later as “external pointer is not valid”.
  • bool_stabilize_underdispersion keeps nuisance_vec a named numeric vector on both branches.
  • Column standard deviations of a sparse matrix are computed from the stored non-zeros without cancellation; the two-pass formula returned NaN for a column with a large mean and a small variance.
  • compute_pvalue() stops when an arm has one individual (the Welch degrees of freedom were zero and every p-value NaN), and multtest() stops when no estimator can fit a null and warns when the null has no spread.
  • fisher_test(verbose = TRUE) prints its summary; the string was built and discarded.

Input validation

New errors that name the cause, in place of failures far downstream:

  • A rank-deficient design is refused by initialize_esvd() and by the reparameterization, naming the aliased columns. Including an indicator for every individual, or for every level of a factor, causes this. The 2024 ASD design of the articles is rank deficient (Seqbatch and region are determined by Capbatch); 1.0.1.07 fit it anyway.
  • eSVD() refuses a batch_var_prefix matching no variable, variables missing from the Seurat object, a case_control_var whose values are not the two case_control_levels, k above the number of genes, all-zero genes, individuals in both arms, an arm with fewer than two individuals, and individuals with fewer than min_cells_per_individual cells.
  • The posterior’s settings are validated once, for compute_posterior(), compute_test_per_gene() and eSVD() alike: a boolean that is not one TRUE or FALSE, bool_adjust_covariates = TRUE together with bool_covariates_as_library = TRUE, and a non-positive alpha_max, library_min or pseudocount. nuisance_lower_quantile = NULL means no floor on both paths; it used to empty the vector of rates.
  • initialize_esvd() refuses NA or non-finite covariates and a k that is not a positive integer; opt_esvd() refuses NA in any input; format_covariates() names a factor with one level; the family constructor names an unknown family; .svd_safe() refuses a mean_vec or sd_vec of the wrong type or length.

Packaging

  • DESCRIPTION: the title and description are rewritten for CRAN and cite the paper; ‘Rmpfr’ and ‘sparseMatrixStats’ are no longer needed (the log-scale p-values and the sparse standard deviations replace them); ‘Rcpp’ moved from Depends to Imports; ‘stats’ and ‘utils’ are imported; ‘devtools’, ‘EnhancedVolcano’ and ‘npregfast’ leave Suggests and ‘ggplot2’, ‘ggrepel’, ‘rmarkdown’ and ‘withr’ join it; biocViews is dropped and BugReports added.
  • LICENSE is the two-line CRAN form for MIT, and NEWS.md and cran-comments.md exist.
  • NAMESPACE exports only the functions marked @export; the pattern export that exposed every non-dot object, including the raw Rcpp bindings that take external pointers, is gone.
  • Every exported function has documentation and a runnable example, and about 35 misleading comments and roxygen descriptions in R/ and src/ are corrected.
  • The test suite grows from 12 files and 31 blocks to 29 files, 298 blocks and about 2,100 expectations, with fixtures regenerated by tests/assets/data_generation.R (the shipped fixture shrinks from 10 MB to 0.4 MB).
  • The vignette eSVD2.Rmd runs without ‘Seurat’ or ‘ggplot2’ (those chunks are skipped) and gains sections on report_results(), the over-dispersion diagnostics and recompute_pvalue(). The two ASD tutorials, which need multi-gigabyte downloads, are pkgdown articles under vignettes/articles/ and were rerun under 1.2.0 through eSVD_helper(), with the diagnostic plots and a comparison of caps.
  • .Rbuildignore keeps the collaboration material (additional_context/, the CLAUDE*.md and HISTORY_*.md notes, .githooks/, oldcode/) out of the tarball; it stays on GitHub.

eSVD2 1.0.1.07

The master branch on GitHub from April 2026 until 1.2.0: small fixes on top of 1.0.0.
